question: A 35-year-old man is brought to the emergency department by his wife because of a 1-week history of progressive confusion, myalgia, and nausea. His wife says that he first reported headaches and fatigue 10 days ago, and since then “he has not been himself”. He has refused to drink any liquids for the last day. Two months ago, he helped his neighbor remove a raccoon's den from her backyard. He appears agitated. His temperature is 100.8°F (38.2°C). Examination shows excessive drooling. Muscle tone and deep tendon reflexes are increased bilaterally. Administration of which of the following is most likely to have prevented this patient's condition?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Exposure to raccoon feces -> possible infection with rabies virus -> rabies encephalitis -> symptoms of confusion, myalgia, nausea -> refusal to drink liquids -> dehydration -> agitation -> increased muscle tone and deep tendon reflexes -> possible rabies infection from raccoon exposure -> 70%
enhanced_information: Exposure to raccoon feces can lead to possible rabies infection, presenting with symptoms of confusion, myalgia, nausea, and dehydration. Agitation, increased muscle tone, and deep tendon reflexes can also be seen. The most likely intervention to prevent this patient's condition would have been a live attenuated rabies vaccine, which could have provided protection against rabies virus infection.
analysis: The patient's symptoms and history of exposure to raccoon feces suggest a possible rabies infection. The presentation of confusion, myalgia, nausea, dehydration, agitation, increased muscle tone, and hyperreflexia align with rabies encephalitis. The most effective preventive measure against rabies is a live attenuated vaccine, which could have provided protection in this case.
